frozenBy: implementation lane, before tuning temporal retrieval against bench/dataset/dev.json and before any protocol-v2 held-out run
status: This file is written BEFORE tuning. Any change to representation, embedding, ranking, thresholds, candidate limits, temporal scoring constants, or dataset composition requires bumping protocolVersion and re-deriving protocolHash via `node bench/freeze-protocol.mjs --write`, and invalidates prior held-out results against the old hash. If bench/dataset/test.json is ever read by a tuning script, the holdout is burned and a new, unused holdout must be constructed before any further claim is made.

developmentTarget.statement: At least 75% Hit@5 on answerable (non no-evidence) semantic-archaeology cases in bench/dataset/dev.json, with exact-identifier (category=exact_identifier) performance reported SEPARATELY and not folded into the 75% figure.
developmentTarget.isA: A provisional product-quality floor used to pick a default configuration before the held-out run.
developmentTarget.isNotA: A statistical claim. With 20 answerable dev cases (24 dev cases minus 4 dev no-evidence cases), a single-point Hit@5 estimate carries wide uncertainty; do not report a confidence interval implying more precision than a 20-item sample supports.
developmentTarget.selectionRule: The smallest/cheapest candidate embedding model meeting the target is the default unless a documented, material gain on dev data justifies the extra cost (extra cost = latency, disk, or memory -- see bench/perf/run.mjs).

ranking.method: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) over the lexical (FTS) and semantic (vector) branches.
ranking.rrfConstantRationale: 60 is the constant from the original Cormack et al. RRF paper and is the de facto default in hybrid-search literature; not tuned against this dataset. Changing it would require re-freezing this protocol.
ranking.formula: score(doc) = sum over branches b where doc appears in b's ranked list of 1 / (rrfConstant + rank_b(doc)), 1-indexed rank.
ranking.commitCollapse: Evidence-level hits are grouped to their owning commit before RRF; a commit's rankScore is computed from its best rank in each branch, per docs/spec.md section 14. This file does not restate the grouping algorithm -- src/search/ owns it -- it only pins the constant and candidate limits used when bench measures it.

temporal.identityConstraint: When no temporal intent is detected the constraint type is 'none', temporal(c) is exactly 1 for every commit, and w is 0, so final(c) is bit-identical to fusedRRF(c). A golden test asserts that a non-temporal query produces byte-identical ranking to the pre-temporal code path.
temporal.exponentRationale: Confidence scales the temporal term rather than gating it, so a misparsed intent costs rank instead of destroying the result set.
temporal.noRecencyPrior: There is no always-on recency boost. Re3 (arXiv:2509.01306) measures recall@1 falling from 0.742 to 0.268 under a fixed relevance/recency weight; a fixed prior is a known failure mode, not a conservative default.
temporal.ordinalsFromAncestry: first/last/removed answers are resolved from validity intervals ordered by commit ancestry (topological order), never by committer or author timestamp, because rebases and cherry-picks rewrite timestamps.
temporal.tunedOn: bench/dataset/dev.json ONLY. The held-out split must never inform a constant in that file.

structuralExpansion.what: From the top-N semantic seeds, commits linked by the lineage table (same path key with overlapping line ranges; interval endpoints of tokens in seed evidence) are added to the candidate pool, tagged matchedBy='linked' with a hop-count linkDistance, entering scoring at the seed's fused score discounted by hops.
structuralExpansion.why: Terse originating commits ('add vquic', 'initial streams') never enter a semantic candidate pool on their own. This is the observed external-v2 failure and a wider top-k does not fix it; only structure does.
structuralExpansion.disabledWhen: constraint.type === 'none'. Ordinary queries see no expansion at all.

candidateLimits.note: Both branches are queried for up to 50 candidate records (commit or evidence records, per the storage eligibility filter) before RRF fusion and commit collapse. This mirrors the SearchRequest.limit ceiling of 50 in src/types.ts.
candidateLimits.resultLimitForMetricsNote: Hit@1/3/5 and Recall@5 are computed over the top 5 returned commits. MRR is computed over the full returned ranking up to resultLimitForMetrics.

perRunBudgets.generatedTokensNote: Generated and input tokens are summed across every step_finish event and recorded without an execution cap. Output length is a measured resource, not a reason to truncate an otherwise valid trial. Wall time and tool-call counts remain actively enforced by the runner (bench/agents/runner.mjs) via a deadline timer and a tool-call counter over the parsed event stream.
perRunBudgets.appliesTo: Each individual OpenCode trial (one arm x one task x one repetition) in Benchmark B.

A.name: baseline
A.tools: Normal OpenCode built-in tools: shell, file read/edit, ripgrep, tests, and native Git history commands (git log, git show, git blame, git log -S, git log -G). No zg. No git why.

B.name: workspace
B.tools: Arm A + Zvec-Grep (zg) over the current task workspace. No git why.
B.status: RUNNABLE. zg (Zvec-Grep) 0.2.2 is installed and verified by `git why doctor`. The runner builds the zg index in the trial clone and asserts `zg status --check-ready` before the trial; a failure is recorded as treatment_error, never as a silent skip.

C.name: workspace+history
C.tools: Arm A + the identical zg setup from arm B + git why over the permitted history.
C.status: RUNNABLE, same zg dependency as arm B, plus a `git why index` built in the clone with `git why status --check-ready` asserted before the trial.

D.name: history
D.tools: Arm A + git why over the permitted history, without zg.
D.status: RUNNABLE. Requires a built dist/cli/main.js and a prebuilt index in the trial clone.

secondaryComparisons: (C - B) - (D - A) interaction, descriptive only, not attributed entirely to Git Why

modelCalibration.runs: at most 2 candidates x 2 neutral tasks
modelCalibration.purpose: confirm actual free availability and tool use

pilot.runs: 28 frozen tasks (16 coding, 6 rubric, 6 temporal) x 4 arms x 2 fresh trials = 224
pilot.purpose: first paired usefulness comparison across coding, blinded rubric, and temporal-history strata

optionalReplication.runs: same 28-task pilot with one selected DevPass model
optionalReplication.status: authorized by the human for this evaluation cohort, subject to billedModelBudget

optionalLargerStudy.status: not run; only after pilot identifies a reason to expand

concurrency.note: Two concurrent OpenCode sessions TOTAL across all arms, not two per arm. Arm order is randomized within each task/trial block and arms are interleaved so time-of-day/provider load does not systematically favor any one arm.

billedModelBudget.verified: `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4-flash` returns a response on this machine, 2026-09-10.
billedModelBudget.catalogPriceAtApproval: not recorded by `opencode models`; the CLI does not expose per-token pricing. Cost is therefore measured from observed token usage per trial, not predicted. Recording it as unknown rather than inventing a figure.
billedModelBudget.supersedes: The prior zero-spend rule and the opencode/big-pickle free-cohort calibration in bench/results/agents/model-calibration.json.
billedModelBudget.recalibrationNote: The pilot model changed, so the earlier calibration no longer describes the model under test. Recalibrate before the pilot and record the result. The calibration must still be performed BEFORE any arm comparison, so that the model is not chosen by which arm it happens to favour.
billedModelBudget.note: A billed model does not relax any other rule. Token and cost accounting must still sum across ALL step_finish events and be cross-checked against the session row in the profile's opencode.db, and must be null rather than zero when unavailable -- a billed run recording zero cost is a reporting bug, not a free run.

datasetComposition.paraphraseRule: Paraphrases of the same underlying change stay in the same split. This dataset does not include deliberate paraphrase pairs (each case targets a distinct underlying commit or commit pair); the rule is recorded here for any future dataset extension.
datasetComposition.externalValidity: bench/dataset/external.json: 12 hand-verified cases over expressjs/express and axios/axios (both MIT-licensed), 6 dev / 6 test, pinned cutoff SHAs and ancestry-verified relevant SHAs. See that file's 'notBlinded' field.

agentTaskCorpus.historyFloor: Every synthetic task fixture has at least 120 commits; pinned external fixtures have 2,287-30,000 commits.
agentTaskCorpus.visibility: The committed public catalogs contain only task id/kind/stratum/version/commit count. Prompts, answer labels, hidden tests, private manifests, task repositories, and review packets are evaluator-only state outside the worktree.

ablation.name: summary-only vs summary+diff-evidence
ablation.scope: development split only (bench/dataset/dev.json), never run against the held-out split
ablation.purpose: Tests whether ingesting diff/evidence records earns its complexity over indexing commit summaries (subject+body) alone.

commitLevel: Recall@5 (multi-relevant, correct denominator = count of ALL relevant SHAs for the case, not 1)
metrics.noEvidenceHandling: No-evidence cases are excluded from Hit@k/Recall@k/MRR (there is no relevant SHA to rank). They are reported separately: what the system actually returned (top-k commits), and whether a fabricated-sounding rationale would be unsupported by that evidence.
metrics.denominatorWarning: "At least one relevant hit in the top 5" is Hit@5, not Recall@5. Recall@5 for a case with N relevant SHAs is (relevant SHAs found in top 5) / N.

temporal.exactFirst: Fraction of when-introduced cases whose returned `answer.sha` equals the labelled introducedSha. Scored on the `answer` field, not on the ranked list, because they are different claims.
temporal.timelinePrecisionRecall: Against the labelled orderedChain, over the returned timeline episodes.
temporal.nonTemporalRegression: MRR on the non-temporal cases, reported before and after the temporal term. The gate is no worse than 0.005 absolute on dev. The temporal-QA survey (arXiv:2505.20243) recommends mixing temporal and non-temporal cases precisely so this can be shown.
temporal.baselineToBeat: 4 of 15 Hit@1 on the external-v2 'when first' probes under protocol v1.

comparisons: Vector only, per candidate embedding model
Hybrid (RRF per this protocol), per candidate embedding model

supersedes.note: The v1 hash was a literal string with no generator; re-deriving it from the v1 content yields sha256:29ce6b89bbdc23cc333f024bbd5999ecbd0fb3dd998671240fbbcecac23e0c71, so it never certified anything. bench/freeze-protocol.mjs now derives the hash from the protocol's own content and `mise run check` verifies it. Retrieval results recorded against protocol v1 remain valid as v1 results; they are NOT comparable to v2 results, because v2 changes ranking (RANKING_VERSION 1 -> 2, temporal term) and adds a stratum.
supersedes.invalidatedAgentPilot: bench/results/agents/pilot-2026-09-09T23-13-53-652Z was deleted, not superseded. Eight independent harness defects (workspace re-rooting, no index in any trial workspace, evaluator material reachable, task answers written into src/, 3-commit task repos with answers in the prompts, token accounting reading only the final step_finish event, an uncalibrated billed model, and rubric trials mixed into pass counts). It must not be cited.

strata.coding: Revert-and-reapply tasks plus current-code, simple-edit and no-evidence controls. Graded by the upstream test from the fix commit. pass is boolean.
strata.rubric: Judged by a blinded rubric. pass is null and MUST NOT enter any pass-rate numerator or denominator. Mixing rubric trials into per-arm pass counts was defect 8 of the invalid v1 pilot.
strata.temporal: When-introduced / when-removed / history-of questions, labelled with introducedSha, removedSha and an orderedChain in ancestry order.
strata.aggregationRule: Every reported rate carries an explicit numerator and denominator, per stratum and per arm. No rate is reported over a mixed-stratum denominator.

hashChangeLog.change: Recorded the owner's approval of billed DevPass model llmgateway/deepseek-v4-flash for the agent pilot, replacing the zero-spend rule.
hashChangeLog.doesNotAffect: Retrieval semantics: representation, embedding, ranking, candidate limits and temporal scoring constants are untouched. Retrieval results recorded against the immediately preceding v2 hash remain directly comparable and are NOT invalidated by this re-freeze.
hashChangeLog.noPilotResultsInvalidated: No valid agent-pilot trial existed at the time of this change -- every trial on disk was invalid -- so nothing was lost.
